#### WP-CPM round 3 — plan and its QC-3 attack (session 7, 2026-09-29, base `0b45eb28`)

**Order kept.** The corpus rebuild (the instrument) and the reproducer re-run ran first; this plan was then written
and every assumption below attacked on the pristine tree BEFORE any finder was spawned. No probe family ran before
the plan.

**Scope (charter §10 CPM, what sessions 5 and 6 left):** round 3 of probe families, aimed at the saturation rule
(two consecutive probe families with no new CANDIDATE). Session 5 ran F-RES, F-META, F-EDGE-L, F-EDGE-C; session 6
ran F-PCF, F-DRAG, F-SSI, F-EDGE2, F-META2, F-LEADS. None of the five families below is a third pass of those:

1. **F-FAMB** — ADR-0251's family B (the counterfactual re-solve: `/driving-path`, its tiers panel,
   `/api/driving-path`, `/export/{fmt}/driving-tiers/{name}`, `/evolution` + corridor under the options, all through
   `web/evolution.py:151` `_optioned_versions`), the SSI "Separate parallel paths" decomposition
   (`web/driving.py:340-379` → `static/path.js`), and the two session-6 route leads (the `/api/driving` inactive
   target; `/evm`'s refusal notice).
2. **F-DAY** — the working day on a schedule whose day is not 480 minutes, measured on EVERY served surface (routes
   enumerated from `create_app`, every export format, the exhibits CLI): the committed `TP2_Bridge_4x10_Calendar.xml`
   (600) and hand-built 420 / 600 / 1440-minute project days with a 480 control. CPM-018's three Path Analysis sites,
   CPM-015 and CPM-017 are screened out as known.
3. **F-CALG** — calendar-arithmetic algebra: `engine/cpm.py`'s converter pair and wall-path helpers and
   `model/calendar.py`, as a seeded property battery over generated calendars and instants, each property quoted from
   its docstring before it runs, each violation reduced to a hand case; MPXJ 16.2.0's `ProjectCalendar` as an
   alternative witness only.
4. **F-TWIN** — what session 6 designed or identified but never reddened: R8 duality on a reflection-symmetric
   non-continuous week; the wall-path variants of CPM-030 / CPM-031; the twin sites of CPM-034 (`cpm.py:2954`,
   `:3168`) and CPM-032 (`path_evolution.py:156`); the lagged-SF role spelling into a 24-hour task.
5. **F-RT** — the tool's own Save `.json` round trip (charter IMP probe, never run on the committed tree) judged on
   CPM figures: every committed schedule through the SERVED route (`/upload` → `/download/{name}.json` → `/upload`)
   and the library pair, compared field by field and by CPM / driving slack / metrics / the rendered grid.

**Orchestration:** one workflow per wave; the workflow's concurrency cap on this 4-CPU container is min(16, 4 − 2) =
2 agents, inside the charter's three. Wave 9 = the five finders. Wave 10 = claim-only verifier packets, then one
assembler per claim; the lead's teeth last. Every result is written to `$S/audit/wave-<n>/` before its agent
returns. JVM / port work behind `flock $S/locks/jvm.lock`.

**Rulings set before the finders run (so no triage is invented after the fact):**

- **Twin / surface rule.** A new site or surface whose root cause AND fix shape are those of a retained class is
  recorded as an instance extension of that class (`DUPLICATE-OF <ID>`, sites listed, its repair unit's scope noted
  as widened) — never a new class. A distinct mechanism is a new CANDIDATE. The lead rules on every "possible
  extension" flag before a verifier is spent.
- **Lead observations** handed to a finder are testimony: each needs the finder's own red, control and census, and
  any class that grows from one gets a SECOND claim-only verifier (session 6's P8 rule).
- **Saturation.** A family that returns 0 CANDIDATEs after its full population is recorded with its reach; WP-CPM
  closes only if two consecutive families (in this plan's order) return 0 new CANDIDATEs.

written and every assumption below attacked on the pristine tree BEFORE any finder was spawned. No census pass ran
before the plan.

**Scope (charter §10 CPM, what session 5 left):** the six modules session 5 did not probe — `engine/driving_path.py`
(250 lines), `engine/path_trace.py` (122), `engine/float_analysis.py` (112), `engine/path_counterfactual.py` (298),

consecutive families with no new CANDIDATE — is unmet).

**Probe families (six finders, one lane slice each, at most three in flight; the harness allows two):**

   written out; the SSI Drag columns in the committed Directional Path workbooks; every display surface that prints

   constructed ground truth (take a committed schedule, apply one known change to a critical activity, require the

   Directional Path workbook (25 `.xlsx`) and the six SSI goldens against `compute_driving_slack` on the matching
   schedule, per field (driving slack days, path membership, tier, drag), every non-exact class mapped to a home.
4. **F-LEADS** — the five carried leads (L-CPM-a, CPM-005's mirror, R-77 head 5307, the −960 second day with a JVM
   probe under the lock, F-META R3).
5. **F-META2** — second-round metamorphic relations, each justified from an authority before use (see Q8).
6. **F-EDGE2** — second-round edge matrix: what session 5's edge finders did not reach (SF links, negative SS / FF
   lags, deadlines, inactive tasks, level-of-effort / hammocks, out-of-sequence progress, resume / stop, cycles,
   multiple starts / ends, summaries with logic beyond CPM-008).

## How to read this ledger

- **Where the records live.** Every figure below is copied from a session record: `audit/LEAD-DECISIONS.md`
  (the lead's validation record — authoritative where records disagree), `audit/ID-MAP.json`, the finder
  records (waves 0–1), the verifier verdicts (wave 2), the teeth and exposure records (wave 3), the lead's
  second-verification tables, and the gate outputs. `$S` abbreviates the session scratchpad
  (`/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/a499c922-7df2-5cb5-a61f-b1862e5269c9/scratchpad`). **Scratch vanishes with the
  container**: the red commands are quoted exactly as they were run (so a reader can see what was measured),
  but the durable, re-runnable form of every red is the finding's reproducer, which builds its inputs inline
  or from committed fixtures at the stated sha. This is a known departure from the charter's "never a pointer
  to scratch" working rule (§3) and is recorded here rather than hidden.
- **Quoting.** Long records are clipped with "…"; a clip never splices two quotes together. A field with no
  record reads **not recorded**. Anything one party has not confirmed reads **UNVERIFIED**.
- **Blocks.** One block per CONFIRMED-DEFERRED class (47 in session 1; after session 2: 46 retained blocks — 45 CONFIRMED-DEFERRED + 1 FIXED-UPSTREAM — and TST-003's block moved under Non-confirmed records; session 5: 56 retained blocks — 55 CONFIRMED-DEFERRED + 1 FIXED-UPSTREAM — with lane CPM and IMP-006 / IMP-007 added; session 6: 84 retained blocks — 83 CONFIRMED-DEFERRED + 1 FIXED-UPSTREAM — with CPM-010..034, IMP-010, DOC-017 and lane UI added; a session-6 block names its finder, and carries a second claim-only verifier where the class grew from a lead observation). "Verification 1" is the independent verifier
  (fresh context, claim-only packet, charter §6.2); "Verification 2" is the lead's own re-run (§6.3).
  "Teeth" is the `prove-able-to-fail` three-part proof run by the wave-3 assemblers in clones of the base
  (§6.5). Fix sketches, moving pins and exposure windows appear for T1, T2 and LAW-1 only (§6.6).
- **Counting.** Classes, not instances (§5): each block carries its measured instance count and census method.
- **Randomized probes.** No finder, verifier or reproducer record in this session uses a random seed; every
  block's seed field therefore reads "none". (Session 5: no finding rests on a randomized probe, so every session-5 block's seed also reads "none"; finder F-EDGE-C's record lists one seeded crash / hang fuzz — seeds 20260925 and 7, 1,200 schedules, 0 crash — see the Session 5 section.) ## Status legend — read this before trusting a row

Definitions from the charter (§4, §5), plus the two session-2 words at the end; the ledger uses no other status words.

| status | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **CANDIDATE** | a finder's claim with claim, verbatim authority, red, control and class census persisted to disk (§6.1); not yet verified |
| **REPRODUCED** | an independent verifier with fresh context reproduced the claim from scratch at the sha and attempted refutation (§6.2) |
| **CONFIRMED-DEFERRED** | the campaign's terminal state for a real defect: "reproduced, reproducer committed, fix priced in the plan" (§5) — this session: reproducer produced as a file, not committed (MODE); session 4 committed them, and session 5 commits its ten on the campaign branch; session 6 commits its 28 on `claude/gallant-newton-yh75tr` |
| **UNVERIFIED** | "a verification is missing or incomplete; re-queued" (§5); no verdict is not a verdict |
| **REFUTED** | the claim was probed and did not hold; the probe is cited |
| **NON-REPRODUCED** | an honest probe could not produce the claimed symptom; what would settle it is stated |
| **UNVERIFIABLE** | cannot be settled from this side; the settling observation is named |
| **ARTIFACT-GATED** | needs something only the operator can produce (a fresh Fuse or SSI export, an MS Project run, a Windows observation); at most PLAUSIBLE here; goes to the ASKS file (§4) |
| **DUPLICATE-OF** `<ID>` | the same defect class as an existing row (this or a prior audit), cited by its ID |
| **HELD-BY** `<ADR>` | measured, and deliberately left by a documented decision whose premise still holds (§4 "not errors") |
| **FIXED-UPSTREAM** | (session 2) the defect was reproduced at the base and is gone on the current `origin/main`, closed by a named upstream commit; kept in the register, excluded from the repair plan, its reproducer converted to a passing pin with a measured negative control |
| **WITHDRAWN** | (session 2) the claim was measured true but falls under charter §4 "not errors" (disagreement with a documented deliberate decision whose premise still holds); omitted from the register count, its record kept under Non-confirmed records, its reproducer removed |

This session's tally (LEAD-DECISIONS): **47 CONFIRMED-DEFERRED** classes · **3 HELD-BY** · **2 REFUTED** ·
**1 DUPLICATE-OF R-32** · **1 UNVERIFIED** candidate (UI-001) · no NON-REPRODUCED, UNVERIFIABLE or
ARTIFACT-GATED verdicts (one sub-question inside a REFUTED record — SSI's display of a sub-day negative slack —
stays UNVERIFIED with its settling observation named). The 50 claims sent to verifiers in 12 packets all
returned REPRODUCED, several NARROWED; where a verifier narrowed a claim, its scope wins.

**Session-2 tally (falsification pass, LEAD-DECISIONS-2):** 47 in → **0 REFUTED · 44 NOT-REFUTED · 3 NARROWED · 1 FIXED-UPSTREAM (DOC-014) · 1 WITHDRAWN (TST-003)** → **46 retained, 45 open**; HELD-BY 3, REFUTED 2 and the DUPLICATE (now CLOSED UPSTREAM, verified) unchanged; UI-001 promoted to CANDIDATE; two new UNVERIFIED leads.

## Testimony-risk tiers — quoted verbatim

From `docs/STATE/AUDIT-2026-08-27-REPORT.md` §0, lines 24–31 (read at 8c71c639), unchanged (charter §5:
"Quote that table into the ledger; do not paraphrase it"):

| tier | what a wrong item costs on the stand |
| --- | --- |
| **T1** | a FIGURE the analyst would cite is, or could be, WRONG — the engine, a metric basis, a CPM rule, a parity leg |
| **T2** | the figure is right but could be MISREAD — mislabelled, misattributed, a wrong unit, an unstated basis, a defaulted value that looks measured |
| **T3** | the RECORD — Law 1's transaction log, what the tool discloses about itself, the documents that describe it |
| **T4** | CONTROLS and RENDERING that could hide evidence or mislead a reader — a dead control, a race, an overflow, a stale header |
| **T5** | PROCESS — CI, instruments, tests that could not fail, figures of unknown provenance |
| **T6** | ORGANIZATIONAL — decisions that are not engineering's to make |

Law 1 bypasses additionally carry the flag **LAW-1** and are disclosed like a T1 (charter §5, §6.6).

### A0923-AI-002 · AI · T1 · CONFIRMED-DEFERRED

**Claim.** At 8c71c639, a sign flip written with U+2212, U+2013 or seven other dash-like code points passes every figure gate — strict and annotate Ask ('−134' ACCEPTED with no footer where ASCII '-134' is DISCARDED against the engine's '+134'), the dual-model cross-check, the Executive Briefing polish ('−143 workday(s) … (ahead of plan)') and /api/translate ('+12' → '−12') — and the engine's own text 'DCMA-14' seeds '-14' as a citable value; ADR-0131:58-60 (M6) requires a sign flip to change the figure multiset and fail.

*Scope (the verifier's narrowing, adopted):* Verifier: broader than claimed (9 non-ASCII dash code points bypass); narrative polish had no signed figure to flip, so there the measured case is a sign introduced on an unsigned figure.

- **Authority** — docs/adr/0131-audit-cluster-remediation-batch1.md:58-60: '7. **M6 — figure-gate is sign-aware.** `ai/citations._FIGURE_RE` gains an optional leading `-`, so a rephrase that flips `-5 days` (ahead) to `5 days behind` changes the multiset and forces the verbatim fallback. Sign is load-bearing in schedule forensics (variance / float / slip direction).' (read at 8c71c639) (+2 further authority citation(s) in the finder record)
- **Basis** — ENGINE≠ORACLE — A2 (the repo's own contract, independent of the code under test): ADR-0131:58-60, CLAUDE.md:230-231, ADR-0239:19-22; +134 re-derived by date arithmetic.
- **Red** (as run; `$S` = session scratch):

  ```text
  $ python3 $S/audit/wave-1/F3-AI/harness/probe_b5c_ask_workbook_signflip.py
  $ python3 $S/audit/wave-1/F3-AI/harness/probe_b5_signflip_routes.py
  $ python3 $S/audit/wave-1/F3-AI/harness/probe_b5d_hyphen_seeding.py (each prints to stdout; saved copies: the matching *.out.txt in this directory)
  ENGINE FACT IN THE PROMPT: ... Project2.mspdi.xml 2027-09-14; Project5.mspdi.xml 2028-01-26. From Project2.mspdi.xml to Project5.mspdi.xml that date …
  [strict  ] [CONTROL ascii '-'] model: 'The computed finish moved -134 calendar days across the series.' -> DISCARDED
  [strict  ] [U+2212          ] model: 'The computed finish moved −134 calendar days across the series.' -> ACCEPTED, no footer
  [annotate] [U+2212          ] ... -> ACCEPTED, no footer
  /api/ai/briefing [U+2212 minus    ] polished=True headline: In one sentence: Project5.mspdi.xml is forecast to finish on Wednesday, January 26, 2028 …
  /api/translate   [CONTROL ascii '-'] -> (source kept — translation discarded)
  … (2 more lines in the record)
  ```

- **Control** — ASCII '-' flips are caught everywhere they should be (strict DISCARDED, annotate footnoted, briefing/translation keep the engine text) — the M6 gate works for the ASCII hyphen. ### A0923-CUI-004 · CUI · T3 · CONFIRMED-DEFERRED

### A0923-WEB-004 · WEB · T4 · latent in the tree; common in operator file names · CONFIRMED-DEFERRED

**Claim.** At 0b45eb28 a schedule uploaded under a file name carrying any code point above U+00FF — outside ISO-8859-1: an en dash (`Bridge – Rev 3.xml`), the Word / Windows apostrophe (`Owner’s Update 3.xml`, U+2019), an em dash, Cyrillic, CJK — loads (POST /upload 303) and gets a **Save .json** link on the dashboard (web/app.py:1811 renders it for EVERY loaded key), but GET /download/{key}.json answers HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error': `download_json` (app.py:1967-1978) puts the key through `_safe_filename` (app.py:8125-8127, strips only `"\\\r\n`) into `Content-Disposition`, and Starlette raises UnicodeEncodeError encoding the header latin-1 (starlette/responses.py:61). An ASCII name and an ISO-8859-1 name (`Café Plan.xml`) answer 200 with the re-openable JSON — the boundary is ISO-8859-1, not ASCII. docs/USER-GUIDE.md:75-76 and README.md:70 promise every loaded schedule a Save .json. No figure is wrong; a documented control dies as an unnamed 500.

*Scope (verifier P2, adopted):* "Reproduced as stated, boundary confirmed exactly at ISO-8859-1 … in-process raw ASGI AND over the wire (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1) … Precision: a TestClient-only check mis-reports the Latin-1 control as a 500 (httpx decodes response headers as UTF-8 and raises client-side), so the raw-ASGI / wire measurement is required for the control." Latent in the tree (0 of 106 tracked schedule-extension names carry a code point above U+00FF); common in real operator file names.

- **Authority** (verbatim, clipped) — A2 (product contract): docs/USER-GUIDE.md:75-76 "with **Open report**, **Card**, and **Save .json** (exports the normalised schedule as a / re-openable `.json`, calendar and holidays included)."; README.md:70 "Each schedule lists **Open report** and **Save .json**."; app.py:1811 `f' &middot; <a href="/download/{quote(name)}.json">Save .json</a></td></tr>'`; app.py:8126 "Strip characters that could break out of the Content-Disposition filename (header hygiene)." (header safety is `_safe_filename`'s stated job). Starlette encodes header values latin-1 (responses.py:61, read in the traceback). RFC 6266 `filename*` named as the fix shape only, not fetched.
- **Basis** — ENGINE≠ORACLE (the finder's label): the oracle is the operator-facing contract plus the HTTP status itself, independent of the route code; no numeric oracle is needed. Controls: ASCII and Latin-1 names save 200 and re-open model-equal on the same tree.

### A0923-CPM-001 · CPM · T1 · in committed corpus · CONFIRMED-DEFERRED

**Claim.** At 19173728, loading tests/fixtures/golden/fuse_hardfile/Hard_File_updated3.mspdi.xml.gz into the app (create_app(SessionState()) + POST /upload) and requesting GET /path, /briefing and /brief displays the schedule-logic (CPM) project finish as 12/11/2026 (Friday December 11, 2026 / 2026-12-11), whereas MS Project's stored project FinishDate (and its latest stored task Finish) is 2026-12-12T17:00:00 and the engine's own CPMResult.project_finish_wall is 2026-12-12 17:00. Same shape on the 24-hour snapshot (Hard_File_updated3_24hr: stored FinishDate 2026-11-19T01:00:00, displayed 2026-11-18).

*Scope (the lead's, from both verifications):* every page that prints the CPM project finish renders `offset_to_datetime(project_finish)` and ignores `CPMResult.project_finish_wall`: Hard_File_updated3 shows 12/11/2026 where MS Project, Acumen Fuse, SSI and the engine's own wall read Sat 2026-12-12 17:00 (24-hour save: 11/18 for 2026-11-19 01:00). Working-day figures (float, the "+26 wd slip") are unaffected — both instants are the same working minute; calendar-date surfaces and calendar-day arithmetic are wrong.

- **Authority** — A1 MS Project's FinishDate (golden line 12, read with ElementTree) = the latest stored task Finish, 2026-12-12T17:00 (UIDs 146 / 411 / 155; UID 146 is 48 elapsed hours, DurationFormat 8, Thu 12-10 17:00 → Sat 12-12 17:00 — Microsoft Learn, DurationFormat element: elapsed time counts non-working time). Witnesses independent of the MPXJ goldens: Acumen Fuse v8.11.0 "Hard_File_updated2 vs update3 Forensic Analysis Report.xlsx", sheet Projects: Hard_File_updated3 Finish 2026-12-12 17:00 (serial 46368.708333), Time Now 2026-10-12 17:00 (the golden's StatusDate), Hard_File_updated2 Finish 2026-11-06 17:00 → a 36-day move; SSI "Hard File updated3_UID_155_Directional_Path_Analysis_2026-7-15.xlsx": UIDs 146, 155, 411 finish Sat 2026-12-12; the 24-hour SSI export: 2026-11-19 01:00. A2 `engine/cpm.py:291-295` (the `project_finish_wall` docstring: "…None when every task follows the project calendar — offset_to_datetime(project_finish) is then exact"); `docs/PARITY-REPORT.md:253` records the file's CPM finish "exact" (2026-12-12) and :254 the 24-hour save's (2026-11-19 01:00) — measured on the wall (`tests/parity/test_hard_file_stored_dates_oracle.py:154-156` pins `project_finish_wall or offset_to_datetime`), i.e. the parity claim is proven on a figure no page prints.
- **Basis** — ENGINE≠ORACLE (the engine's own wall is right; the rendering half is wrong) — MS Project's stored FinishDate, Acumen Fuse's Projects sheet and SSI's directional-path export.
- **Red** (verifier V2's red command, byte-identical to the packet's; the durable form is the reproducer below):

  ```text
  import gzip
  from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
  from schedule_forensics.web.app import create_app
  from schedule_forensics.web.state import SessionState
  xml = gzip.decompress(open('tests/fixtures/golden/fuse_hardfile/Hard_File_updated3.mspdi.xml.gz','rb').read())
  c = TestClient(create_app(SessionState()))
  assert c.post('/upload', files={'files': ('Hard_File_updated3.mspdi.xml', xml, 'text/xml')}).status_code == 200
  html = c.get('/path').text
  ```

### A0923-CPM-026 · CPM · T3 · latent · CONFIRMED-DEFERRED

**Claim.** At 13b13f38, engine/driving_path.py:114 sets DrivingPathBetween.source_slack_days = int(results[source].driving_slack_days) for every connected source, including one ON the target's driving path, although the field's contract (:50-51) is 'in whole working days, when connected (``0`` while it drives)'. Witnesses on committed goldens: Hard_File_updated4_24h source 178 -> target 155 drives (46-activity corridor) with -4,146 min (-8.64 d) and the field reads -8; Hard_File source 323 -> target 321 drives with 479 min (< one working day; driving_slack_days is 2-dp-rounded to 1.00 before int()) and the field reads +1. Class (verifier recount, re-derived here): 2,237 of 41,114 driving (source, target) pairs over every target of the 33 corpus files with <= 400 activities carry a non-zero value, -32 .. +1, on 14 files (the Hard_File family + Jacked_up_Schedule_2); the finder's four-focus sample was 54. Latent: DrivingPathSnapshot.status (:153) prints the field only on the NOT-driving branch, and /driving-path?source=178&target=155 reads 'driving path of 46 activities' -- no displayed figure is wrong today.

*Scope (verifier P4's narrowing, adopted by the assembler):* Mechanism and example reproduce exactly; the population figure '54 pairs, -8 or -12' is a sample, not the class. driving_path_between (engine/driving_path.py:114) returns source_slack_days = int(driving_slack_days) - where driving_slack_days is already rounded to 2 dp - for a DRIVING source too, contrary to the field contract at :50-51 ('0 while it drives'). Example reproduced: Hard_File_updated4_24h source 178 -> target 155, drives=True, connected=True, driving slack -4,146 min (-8.64 d), source_slack_days -8, corridor 46 activities; /driving-path?source=178&target=155 prints 'driving path of 46 activities' and never the -8. ### A0923-CPM-041 · CPM · T2 · latent (premise finding on ADR-0516 D3 / ADR-0355) · CONFIRMED-DEFERRED

**Claim.** At 0b45eb28 every served day figure divides working minutes by the project calendar's DERIVED day — `web/state.py:1703` `per_day = sch.calendar.working_minutes_per_day or 480` (duration / remaining / work / lag days) and `engine/float_analysis.py:78` (total / free float days) — never by the file's own `<MinutesPerDay>` (`Calendar.declared_minutes_per_day`, read only by `engine/msp_filters.py:148`, filter literals). A hand MSPDI declaring 480 (Hours per day = 8) over a 600-minute calendar, via /upload + GET /api/analysis, serves Build 15.0 d for 9,000 min and Permits' total float 9.0 d for 5,400 min — byte-identical to the twin declaring 600 — where the declared day gives 18.75 / 11.25 and the vendored MPXJ 16.2.0 (the model ADR-0355 names) reads 18.75d. Both producers are documented decisions whose stated premise the code does not meet: ADR-0355:67-69 ("exactly mirroring MPXJ's split" — MPXJ converts EVERY duration with the declared setting) and ADR-0516:53-54 ("the tool's reading on the schedule's declared day … its hours-per-day setting" — the code reads the derived day). /analysis says 'Working day 10 h/day (600 min)'; the declared 8 h/day appears nowhere. MS Project's own rendering: UNVERIFIED.

## WP plans as executed — load-bearing assumptions and how each was tested

**Deviation, stated plainly.** Charter §9 requires that "before each WP's first probe, write the WP plan into
the ledger and attack it (QC-3): list its load-bearing assumptions (population, oracle, witness, mechanism)
and test each on the pristine tree." **That was not done first this session.** No WP plan was written into a
ledger before its first probe; the QC-3 attack was instead **folded into the finder / verifier protocol** —
every finder recorded a control, a class census and its own refutation attempts per claim (§6.1), and every
verifier ran the five mandatory refutation attempts per claim (§6.2). The plans below are **reconstructed after
the fact** from those records. What the fold costs: a per-claim attack cannot catch a wrong population or a
missing oracle for a work package as a whole — the clearest case is WP-CPM, whose oracle (the 44-file
stored-value corpus) was never rebuilt, so its differential census never ran. Next sessions should write each
WP plan, with its attacked assumptions, into the ledger before the first probe.

### WP-CPM (session 5) — written and attacked BEFORE its finders (with one recorded deviation)

Session 5 wrote the WP-CPM plan down (a session record) and attacked its eight load-bearing assumptions on the pristine tree
before any finder was spawned — the QC-3 step sessions 1–2 folded into the finder protocol. The plan and its attack
table are inserted verbatim in the "Session 5" section at the top of this ledger ("WP-CPM plan and its QC-3 attack").
Recorded deviation: the corpus rebuild and the first pass of the differential census ran about 30 minutes before the
plan was written. What fell: **P7** ("a date difference on the census is a defect") as a blanket premise — every
non-exact class was mapped to its register row or ADR (finder F-RES) before any could become a CANDIDATE.

### WP-CPM (session 6) — written and attacked BEFORE its finders

Session 6 wrote the WP-CPM continuation plan down and attacked its ten load-bearing assumptions Q1–Q10 on the
pristine tree before any finder was spawned — this time in the charter's order: the corpus rebuild (the instrument)
ran first, and no census pass ran before the plan. The plan and its attack table are inserted verbatim in the
"Session 6" section at the top of this ledger ("WP-CPM plan and its QC-3 attack — inserted verbatim"). What fell:
**Q6** (a day-divisor defect in `drag.py` would be visible on the committed corpus — the project calendar is 480
minutes on 44 of 44 files) and **Q10 for LD-6** (DUPLICATE-OF A0923-CPM-001, not re-filed); Q4 held with a caveat
(a `case.json` is testimony — the finder read the `.xlsx` itself) and Q9 with a condition (no relation ran without a
quoted authority). The lead's correction after wave 7 narrowed Q6 further: the 44-file corpus is a population choice;
the committed tree holds a 600-minute MSPDI (`00_REFERENCE_INTAKE/references/TP2_Bridge_4x10_Calendar.xml`), so the
480-constant class (CPM-018) is live in the committed tree. Two further rules were set by the lead before verification:
three merges (M-DRAGRULE, M-DAY480, M-THANKS) and a second claim-only verifier (P8) for every class that grew from a
lead observation (LD-1 / 2 / 4 / 7). Of the lead's seven plan observations: LD-1, LD-2, LD-4 and LD-7 became classes
(CPM-018, CPM-016, CPM-010, CPM-026); LD-3 produced no candidate (0 drag rows move); LD-5 was REFUTED as a candidate
(ADR-0515's tool-wide half-even rule); LD-6 is DUPLICATE-OF A0923-CPM-001.

### WP-CPM (session 7) — written and attacked BEFORE its finders; round 3, not saturated

Session 7 wrote the WP-CPM round-3 plan down and attacked its thirteen load-bearing assumptions R1–R13 on the pristine
tree before any finder was spawned, in the charter's order: the corpus rebuild (the instrument) and the reproducer
re-run first, the plan second, no probe family before the plan. The plan and its attack table are inserted verbatim in
the "Session 7" section at the top of this ledger ("WP-CPM round 3 — plan and its QC-3 attack"). What fell: **R7**
(the lead's hypothesis that a served day figure silently takes a unit converter's 480 default — every one of the 5
converter calls under `src/schedule_forensics` passes `minutes_per_day`; F-DAY was therefore told to measure RENDERED
figures, not code patterns, and its four classes are all rendered-surface defects a code grep could not have found);
**R10 held with drift** (`path_evolution._predecessors` is at :156, not the :159 session 6 cited); **R13 was left
UNVERIFIED by design** (the two session-6 route leads were not pre-tested by the lead, so the finder stayed
independent of the lead's reading — both became classes, CPM-035 and WEB-003). Two rules were set BEFORE any verdict
was read: the class-boundary rule ("the same class only when the retained class's recorded fix sketch would fix
it") — applied to F-CALG-002 (DUPLICATE-OF CPM-006) and to the four candidates the finders flagged as possible
extensions (all NEW classes: CPM-035's sibling WEB-003, CPM-015 / 017's sibling CPM-042, CPM-032's sibling CPM-045,
CPM-034's sibling CPM-047); and a second claim-only verifier (packet P6) for the three classes that grew from the
lead's own observations (LD-B → CPM-038, LD-D → EXP-001, the LD-C-directed decomposition probe → CPM-039). The plan
also named what the operator's "Try again" later overrode: the charter's stop-spawning rule after an agent death
(recorded above under the orchestration record).
